title: Touch transfer assay for the evaluation of antimicrobial surfaces
author: Johannes K.-M. Knobloch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i59cg96

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Inoculum
steps.instruction: Cultivate Enterococcus faecium ATCC 6057 on Columbia Agar + 5% sheep blood at 36 ± 2 °C under ambient conditions overnight, then inoculate in sterile 0.85% NaCl solution to reach a concentration of approximately 5x10^7 bacteria/mL.

steps.title: Prepare Primary Contaminated Surface (PCS)
steps.instruction: Create the PCS by spreading 200 µl of the bacterial suspension homogenously onto sterilized 5 x 5 cm white matt glaze ceramic tiles (#3709PN00, Villeroy & Boch, Mettlach, Germany).

substeps.instruction: Dry the surfaces for 1 hour in a climate chamber at 22 °C and 50% rH.

steps.title: Prepare Control and Test Surfaces
steps.instruction: Select and disinfect surfaces to be used as the secondary contaminated surface (SCS).

substeps.instruction: Select appropriate control surfaces (e.g., identical materials without antimicrobial components, white matt glaze ceramic tiles #3709PN00, or stainless steel UNS S30400 plates).
Disinfect all surfaces (e.g., using 70% isopropyl alcohol) prior to the assay.

steps.title: Prepare Gloved Fingers
steps.instruction: Equip the test person's forefinger or thumb with moistened sterile cotton gloves worn over disinfected single-use nitrile gloves.

substeps.instruction: Mimic clinical organic soil load by touching Columbia Agar + 5% sheep blood for 10 seconds without pressure.

steps.title: Perform Touch Transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer bacteria from the PCS to the SCS using the prepared gloved fingers.

substeps.instruction: Roll the finger with low pressure on the PCS for 10 seconds without removing the finger.
Roll the finger in the same manner on the respective sterilized test/control surfaces for 10 seconds to create the secondary contaminated surface (SCS).

steps.title: Quantify Surviving Bacteria on SCS
steps.instruction: Perform quantitative culture of the SCS immediately or after 24 hours of incubation at 22 °C and 50% rH.

substeps.instruction: Harvest bacteria by heavy scrubbing with a foam swab (∑-Transwab, Medical Wire, Corsham, UK) moistened with Tryptone Soya Broth (TSB) with LTHTh 373r-20p (Merck, Darmstadt, Germany).
Transfer the swab into 1 ml of TSB with LTHTh.
Streak appropriate volumes of the suspension (or dilutions) onto COS agar plates in double determination.
Incubate plates for 24 hours at 36 ± 2 °C and count colonies.

steps.title: Alternative Quantification for High Activity
steps.instruction: For highly active antimicrobial surfaces where surviving bacteria are low, use Replicate Organism Detection And Counting (RODAC) agar plates containing Tryptone Soya Agar (TSA) with disinhibitor plus (Oxoid, Basingstoke, UK) to increase sensitivity (detection limit 1 cfu/surface).
